jobs.description:
**Research Associate, Internship**
----------------------------------

Open position, Berlin

Internship, 3 months

Location: Berlin (hybrid)

Start: January 2027, or as soon as you can

Format: Full-time internship, 3 months

Level: Master's or PhD student, or equivalent research experience

**Who we are.** Zeitgeist Labs is a new social research institute in Berlin. We are a team of scientists from Stanford, MIT, Max Planck and Charité with experience at McKinsey and in previous startups. This is a unique opportunity to join an early-stage company at its inflection point.

**Problem we solve.** Governments, foundations, NGOs and universities spend trillions every year on programs meant to improve people's lives. The industry that measures whether any of it works is slow and manual: months of fieldwork, hand-coded interviews, a 300 page report that lands 2 years after the program ends. The physical sciences are being accelerated by AI co-scientists. The social sciences are not, yet. In an age of ever-increasing complexity, we are building the tools that allow researchers to tackle the hardest scientific questions of our time: how societies work, and what actually changes them.

**In short. Y**ou own studies end to end, working directly with the founders and our clients. Design the study, run it, analyse the data, create the knowledge. No hand-offs.

**What you'll do.**
-------------------

You work directly with the founders and with our clients: established institutions in the social and health sector. What you design is used in real studies, and the results inform policy and funding decisions.

* Set up full studies on your own: study design, voice agent interviews, structured surveys
* Work with clients directly, from sharpening their research question to presenting the results
* Go deep into the data: analyse interviews and survey responses, write the reports clients act on
* Report product issues to the engineering team and help decide what we build next

**How we work.**
----------------

We are a human-in-the-loop AI company. Everyone here runs a fleet of agents; the human sets the direction, makes the calls and verifies the result. That holds for research as much as for code: agents help you draft, code and analyse, and you answer for the method and for every claim in the report. We care about creativity, critical thinking and solution orientation, not about knowing one particular tool.

**Who we're looking for.**
--------------------------

* Researcher at heart: you have designed and run a piece of research yourself, a thesis, a study, a survey, and you want to do more of it
* Generalist: you are as comfortable in a client call as you are deep in a dataset
* Critical thinker: you question what you read, including what an agent wrote for you, and can explain why a finding holds
* Wants ownership over comfort: small team, short path from your study design to a client's decision

**Bonus points if you have.**
-----------------------------

* A background in the social, political or health sciences, economics or a related field
* Run qualitative or mixed-methods research: interviews, surveys, coding
* Worked with clients, partners or other stakeholders
* A solid understanding of the German language
* An interest in technology and AI. No coding needed, we train you on our tools

**Why Zeitgeist Labs.**
-----------------------

* Ownership of real studies from week one, for established institutions, and work you can name on your CV
* Training on the tech side: voice agents, LLMs and agent workflows
* Daily work with the founders, hybrid in Berlin

**About the interview.**
------------------------

* First call with a founder
* A small case: a working session on a real study design, with your tools

jobs.title: Research Assistant EU-wide characterization soil microbiomes
jobs.description:
**Your job**
------------

Soils are teeming with life. Some soil organisms support plant growth while others use plants as a food source. A notorious example of plant pathogens is root-knot nematodes (RKN) as they have an enormous host range and are widely distributed throughout the subtropical and tropical regions.

Due to global warming, these RKNs are expanding their ranges, and in the framework of a European project named Nem-Emerge we are mapping the current distribution of “tropical” root-knot nematodes. This is not trivial, as they very much look alike.

As a Research Assistant in the European Nem-Emerge project, you will map the current RKN distribution by characterizing samples collected along two major latitudinal transects. In addition, you will also characterize the soil microbial communities that are associated with these nematodes. A combination of long-read DNA sequencing technology and bioinformatics will allow us to map the current distribution and identify microbial antagonists that are associated with these pathogens.

Your work will contribute to a better understanding of range-expanding nematode species and the natural suppressive capacity of the associated soils. Together with researchers across Europe, you will help to generate knowledge that can support more resilient soils and sustainable agriculture.

**Your duties and responsibilities include:**

You will combine advanced molecular techniques, bioinformatics and scientific interpretation. Your main responsibilities are:

* analyzing root-knot nematode communities using long-read DNA sequencing technology;
* analyzing associated microbial assemblages using long-read DNA sequencing technology;
* bioinformatics-based analyses of nematode and microbial communities;
* reporting on results to workpackage leads;
* communication with European project partners about results and interpretation thereof;
* reporting on results to workpackage leads.

**Your team**

You will work with Hans Helder and Aska Goverse - the Nem-Emerge project coordinators -, as well as with two PhDs that are currently employed on the project. Together, you will exchange knowledge, interpret findings and contribute to the project's scientific objectives.

**You will work here**

The full title of the EU Horizon Europe project Nem-Emerge is ‘An integrated set of novel approaches to counter the emergence and proliferation of invasive and virulent soil-borne nematodes’. In this position you will contribute to (a) identifying the current distribution of “tropical” root-knot nematode (RKN) species, as well as (b) mapping the endogenous RKN-suppressive capacity of soils.

**Your qualities**
------------------

You have experience in the DNA-based characterization of (soil) microbiomes, preferably using long-read DNA sequencing technologies, as well as with the associated bioinformatics tools

**You also possess:**

* qualification: MSc in biology, plant sciences, soil sciences or related;
* preferably hands-on experience in (soil) microbiome characterization;
* hands-on bioinformatics skills (relevant R-packages);
* demonstrable (international) project communication skills.

In our international working environment, there is an increasing amount of communication in English. For this position it is about minimally B2 level.

In addition to these first-rate employee benefits, you will of course receive a good salary. Depending on your experience, we offer a gross salary of between € 3,537.- and € 4,673.- for a full-time working week of 38 hours, in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreements for Dutch Universities (CAO-NU) (scale 8). Additionally, a contract for 0,8 FTE can be discussed. We offer you a temporary contract for the duration of one year.

jobs.title: Preclinical evaluation of de- and recellularised muscle constructs in rabbit allograft models
jobs.description:
**Preclinical evaluation of de- and recellularised muscle constructs in rabbit allograft models**
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

*(ref. BAP-2026-707)*
  
*Laatst aangepast: 27/11/26*

This doctoral position will be hosted at KU Leuven and embedded within two closely collaborating research environments:
  
  
BREATHE Lab, part of the Department of Chronic Diseases and Metabolism, is a translational research group led by Prof. Laurens Ceulemans, with expertise in thoracic surgery, transplantation, organ regeneration, and preclinical surgical models.
  
  
The Leuven Intestinal Failure and Transplantation (LIFT) Group is an interdisciplinary clinical and research programme specializing in abdominal wall reconstruction, intestinal failure and transplantation, regenerative surgery, and translational preclinical research.
  
  
Together, these groups offer a unique and highly collaborative research environment at the interface of tissue engineering, regenerative medicine, surgery, transplantation, immunology, biomechanics, and advanced imaging. This setting enables the candidate to engage in truly translational research, spanning from fundamental laboratory studies to clinical application, while collaborating with an international network of academic, clinical, and industrial partners.

##### **Project**

Abdominal wall defects and diaphragmatic hernias affect hundreds of thousands of patients each year, yet current synthetic repair materials often fail to fully integrate with host tissues and may lead to complications or recurrence. This project aims to develop and validate a new generation of **bioengineered muscle grafts** capable of restoring both structural support and biological function.

The doctoral candidate will evaluate **decellularised muscle matrices (DMMs)** and **recellularised muscle constructs** in clinically relevant rabbit models of abdominal wall and diaphragmatic repair. The work will focus on assessing graft integration, tissue remodelling, muscle regeneration, vascularisation, and long-term functionality while characterising the immune mechanisms that drive successful or unsuccessful graft acceptance.

The project combines advanced surgical techniques with comprehensive biological and functional analyses, including biomechanics, multiplex immunofluorescence, vascular and neuromuscular assessment, and pulmonary function measurements. The candidate will investigate both acellular and recellularised grafts and generate critical preclinical evidence supporting their future clinical translation.

Through secondments at **University College London** and **Charles University**, the candidate will receive specialized training in diaphragmatic hernia surgery and advanced in vivo model development. Ultimately, the project will provide essential insights into regenerative muscle reconstruction and contribute to the development of next-generation therapies for complex abdominal wall and diaphragmatic defects.

##### **Profile**

### **Essential requirements**

* Applicant holds a MSc or equivalent degree in Medicine, Veterinary Medicine, or Biomedical Sciences. Candidates with an MD or DVM degree are particularly encouraged to apply.

* Applicant does not hold a PhD degree.

* Applicant did not reside or carry out his/her main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the country of the host organisation for more than 12 months in the 3 years immediately before the recruitment date. Compulsory national service, short stays such as holidays, and time spent as part of a procedure for obtaining refugee status are not considered.

* Applicant demonstrates a high level of proficiency in written and spoken English, which will be assessed with the motivation letter and the interview, respectively.

jobs.description:
**Your role**

Orion Pharma is making strategic investments in challenging R&D areas where our expertise can drive breakthroughs - particularly in cancer therapies.

We are seeking an accomplished Target Discovery Research Scientist to join the Cancer Genomics Target Discovery Research Team. The Target Discovery Research Scientist is a lab-based role focused on evaluating novel therapeutic target ideas and generating experimental evidence to support their advancement. This position combines scientific rigor with hands-on expertise to drive cancer genomics research forward. The ideal candidate will have a strong track record in target identification and validation, preferably within the small molecule space.

**Responsibilities**

**Target Evaluation**  

* Assess and critically evaluate target ideas for biological relevance and therapeutic potential.
* Provide scientific input to ideation sessions and contribute to prioritization decisions.

**Laboratory Validation**  

* Plan and execute laboratory experiments to validate selected targets using state-of-the-art molecular and cellular techniques.
* Ensure experimental design meets high standards of reproducibility and scientific integrity.

**Data Analysis & Reporting**  

* Analyze and interpret experimental results to inform target progression.
* Document findings and communicate outcomes effectively in reports and team meetings.

**Collaboration**  

* Work closely with bioinformatics, translational research, and other cross-functional teams to integrate data-driven insights into validation strategies.

You will work closely with a multidisciplinary team to discover and validate novel cancer targets and help develop first- or best-in-class targets from concept to clinical candidate. This is a unique opportunity to contribute to cutting-edge cancer therapies that can make a real difference for patients.

You will be located in Turku, Finland, and will report to the Target Discovery Team Lead. This is a full-time, temporary, on-site position until the end of June 2027.

**What you can expect from us**

* A chance to work with experienced scientists across Orion’s R&D.
* A dynamic and supportive work environment with opportunities for growth.
* The opportunity to contribute to innovative therapies that improve patients’ lives.

At Orion Pharma, your work creates true impact and well-being for our customers, patients and society at large. Our culture of friendliness, respect, mutual appreciation, and diversity creates a safe working environment where you can strive for excellence. We offer a wealth of career paths and development opportunities that support the development of innovative solutions and improving the quality of life.

Please visit our website to find further information about our values and Orion as an employer https://www.orionpharma.com/careers/working-with-us/.

**What are we looking for?**

**Key Qualifications**  

* Fresh Ph.D. (0–2 years of experience) in Molecular Biology, Cancer Genomics, Genetics, or related field **OR** Master’s degree with 5–6 years of hands-on laboratory experience in oncology research or functional genomics.
* Strong expertise in cell culture, molecular biology, and assay development.
* Experience with CRISPR-based gene editing and functional screening.
* Experience with RNAi, overexpression systems, and knockout cellular models.
* Proficiency in cell-based and biochemical assays, imaging, and high-throughput screening.
* Ability to design and execute complex experiments independently.
* Excellent analytical and communication skills.

**Preferred Skills**  

* Familiarity with computational biology tools and pipelines for target discovery.
* Knowledge of tumor biology and resistance mechanisms.
* Strong ability to interpret large-scale datasets and integrate insights into experimental design.
* Prior experience in pharma or biotech environments with drug discovery exposure is a plus.

Please send your application with the latest CV, cover letter, and salary request in English by December 13, 2026. Please note that we will start reviewing applications during the application period.

For additional details, do not hesitate to contact Dr Daria Bulanova, Acting Target Discovery Lead, via email daria.bulanova@orionpharma.com.

#LI-ORION

Approved medical examination which also includes drug testing is required prior to the employment. We will also carry out a security clearance prior to the employment for the selected person.

Orion’s pharmaceutical innovations are created within its R&D organization. We employ over 400 top professionals in the field of drug discovery and development. We work globally: in Espoo and Turku in Finland, in Nottingham and Cambridge in the UK, and in Cambridge, MA, USA. Orion R&D and the Innovative Medicines business division are dedicated to making a transformation to become a global player in the pain and oncology therapy areas.

----------------------------------

Open position, Berlin

Internship, 3 months

Location: Berlin (hybrid)

Start: January 2027, or as soon as you can

Format: Full-time internship, 3 months

Level: Master's or PhD student, or equivalent research experience

**Who we are.** Zeitgeist Labs is a new social research institute in Berlin. We are a team of scientists from Stanford, MIT, Max Planck and Charité with experience at McKinsey and in previous startups. This is a unique opportunity to join an early-stage company at its inflection point.

**Problem we solve.** Governments, foundations, NGOs and universities spend trillions every year on programs meant to improve people's lives. The industry that measures whether any of it works is slow and manual: months of fieldwork, hand-coded interviews, a 300 page report that lands 2 years after the program ends. The physical sciences are being accelerated by AI co-scientists. The social sciences are not, yet. In an age of ever-increasing complexity, we are building the tools that allow researchers to tackle the hardest scientific questions of our time: how societies work, and what actually changes them.

**In short. Y**ou own studies end to end, working directly with the founders and our clients. Design the study, run it, analyse the data, create the knowledge. No hand-offs.

**What you'll do.**
-------------------

You work directly with the founders and with our clients: established institutions in the social and health sector. What you design is used in real studies, and the results inform policy and funding decisions.

* Set up full studies on your own: study design, voice agent interviews, structured surveys
* Work with clients directly, from sharpening their research question to presenting the results
* Go deep into the data: analyse interviews and survey responses, write the reports clients act on
* Report product issues to the engineering team and help decide what we build next

**How we work.**
----------------

We are a human-in-the-loop AI company. Everyone here runs a fleet of agents; the human sets the direction, makes the calls and verifies the result. That holds for research as much as for code: agents help you draft, code and analyse, and you answer for the method and for every claim in the report. We care about creativity, critical thinking and solution orientation, not about knowing one particular tool.

**Who we're looking for.**

* Researcher at heart: you have designed and run a piece of research yourself, a thesis, a study, a survey, and you want to do more of it
* Generalist: you are as comfortable in a client call as you are deep in a dataset
* Critical thinker: you question what you read, including what an agent wrote for you, and can explain why a finding holds
* Wants ownership over comfort: small team, short path from your study design to a client's decision

**Bonus points if you have.**
-----------------------------

* A background in the social, political or health sciences, economics or a related field
* Run qualitative or mixed-methods research: interviews, surveys, coding
* Worked with clients, partners or other stakeholders
* A solid understanding of the German language
* An interest in technology and AI. No coding needed, we train you on our tools

**Why Zeitgeist Labs.**
-----------------------

* Ownership of real studies from week one, for established institutions, and work you can name on your CV
* Training on the tech side: voice agents, LLMs and agent workflows
* Daily work with the founders, hybrid in Berlin

**About the interview.**
------------------------

* First call with a founder
* A small case: a working session on a real study design, with your tools

This doctoral position will be hosted at KU Leuven and embedded within two closely collaborating research environments:
  
  
BREATHE Lab, part of the Department of Chronic Diseases and Metabolism, is a translational research group led by Prof. Laurens Ceulemans, with expertise in thoracic surgery, transplantation, organ regeneration, and preclinical surgical models.
  
  
The Leuven Intestinal Failure and Transplantation (LIFT) Group is an interdisciplinary clinical and research programme specializing in abdominal wall reconstruction, intestinal failure and transplantation, regenerative surgery, and translational preclinical research.
  
  
Together, these groups offer a unique and highly collaborative research environment at the interface of tissue engineering, regenerative medicine, surgery, transplantation, immunology, biomechanics, and advanced imaging. This setting enables the candidate to engage in truly translational research, spanning from fundamental laboratory studies to clinical application, while collaborating with an international network of academic, clinical, and industrial partners.

##### **Project**

Abdominal wall defects and diaphragmatic hernias affect hundreds of thousands of patients each year, yet current synthetic repair materials often fail to fully integrate with host tissues and may lead to complications or recurrence. This project aims to develop and validate a new generation of **bioengineered muscle grafts** capable of restoring both structural support and biological function.

The doctoral candidate will evaluate **decellularised muscle matrices (DMMs)** and **recellularised muscle constructs** in clinically relevant rabbit models of abdominal wall and diaphragmatic repair. The work will focus on assessing graft integration, tissue remodelling, muscle regeneration, vascularisation, and long-term functionality while characterising the immune mechanisms that drive successful or unsuccessful graft acceptance.

The project combines advanced surgical techniques with comprehensive biological and functional analyses, including biomechanics, multiplex immunofluorescence, vascular and neuromuscular assessment, and pulmonary function measurements. The candidate will investigate both acellular and recellularised grafts and generate critical preclinical evidence supporting their future clinical translation.

Through secondments at **University College London** and **Charles University**, the candidate will receive specialized training in diaphragmatic hernia surgery and advanced in vivo model development. new_jobs.description:
**Your role**

Orion Pharma is making strategic investments in challenging R&D areas where our expertise can drive breakthroughs - particularly in cancer therapies.

We are seeking an accomplished Target Discovery Research Scientist to join the Cancer Genomics Target Discovery Research Team. The Target Discovery Research Scientist is a lab-based role focused on evaluating novel therapeutic target ideas and generating experimental evidence to support their advancement. This position combines scientific rigor with hands-on expertise to drive cancer genomics research forward. The ideal candidate will have a strong track record in target identification and validation, preferably within the small molecule space.

**Responsibilities**

**Target Evaluation**  

* Assess and critically evaluate target ideas for biological relevance and therapeutic potential.
* Provide scientific input to ideation sessions and contribute to prioritization decisions.

**Laboratory Validation**  

* Plan and execute laboratory experiments to validate selected targets using state-of-the-art molecular and cellular techniques.
* Ensure experimental design meets high standards of reproducibility and scientific integrity.

**Data Analysis & Reporting**  

* Analyze and interpret experimental results to inform target progression.
* Document findings and communicate outcomes effectively in reports and team meetings.

**Collaboration**  

* Work closely with bioinformatics, translational research, and other cross-functional teams to integrate data-driven insights into validation strategies.

You will work closely with a multidisciplinary team to discover and validate novel cancer targets and help develop first- or best-in-class targets from concept to clinical candidate. This is a unique opportunity to contribute to cutting-edge cancer therapies that can make a real difference for patients.

You will be located in Turku, Finland, and will report to the Target Discovery Team Lead. This is a full-time, temporary, on-site position until the end of June 2027.

**What you can expect from us**

* A chance to work with experienced scientists across Orion’s R&D.
* A dynamic and supportive work environment with opportunities for growth.
* The opportunity to contribute to innovative therapies that improve patients’ lives.

At Orion Pharma, your work creates true impact and well-being for our customers, patients and society at large. Our culture of friendliness, respect, mutual appreciation, and diversity creates a safe working environment where you can strive for excellence. We offer a wealth of career paths and development opportunities that support the development of innovative solutions and improving the quality of life.

Please visit our website to find further information about our values and Orion as an employer https://www.orionpharma.com/careers/working-with-us/.

**What are we looking for?**

**Key Qualifications**  

* Fresh Ph.D. (0–2 years of experience) in Molecular Biology, Cancer Genomics, Genetics, or related field **OR** Master’s degree with 5–6 years of hands-on laboratory experience in oncology research or functional genomics.
* Strong expertise in cell culture, molecular biology, and assay development.
* Experience with CRISPR-based gene editing and functional screening.
* Experience with RNAi, overexpression systems, and knockout cellular models.
* Proficiency in cell-based and biochemical assays, imaging, and high-throughput screening.
* Ability to design and execute complex experiments independently.
* Excellent analytical and communication skills.

**Preferred Skills**  

* Familiarity with computational biology tools and pipelines for target discovery.
* Knowledge of tumor biology and resistance mechanisms.
* Strong ability to interpret large-scale datasets and integrate insights into experimental design.
* Prior experience in pharma or biotech environments with drug discovery exposure is a plus.

**How to apply**

Please send your application with the latest CV, cover letter, and salary request in English by December 13, 2026. Please note that we will start reviewing applications during the application period.

For additional details, do not hesitate to contact Dr Daria Bulanova, Acting Target Discovery Lead, via email daria.bulanova@orionpharma.com.

#LI-ORION

Approved medical examination which also includes drug testing is required prior to the employment. We will also carry out a security clearance prior to the employment for the selected person.

**Your new team**

Orion’s pharmaceutical innovations are created within its R&D organization. We employ over 400 top professionals in the field of drug discovery and development. We work globally: in Espoo and Turku in Finland, in Nottingham and Cambridge in the UK, and in Cambridge, MA, USA. Orion R&D and the Innovative Medicines business division are dedicated to making a transformation to become a global player in the pain and oncology therapy areas.

Target Discovery Team (Cancer Genomics) is a part of the Cancer Genomics Research Group, one of three scientific units within Oncology Research, a division of Orion’s R&D Organization. Our team is dedicated to the discovery, validation and targeting of therapeutic targets (utilizing small molecule focused modalities), leveraging omics technologies alongside a broad array of biophysical, biochemical, molecular, cellular, and in vivo methods. We strive to develop cutting-edge small molecule therapies with the potential to transform the lives of cancer patients.
